llm.summary: The skill's stated purpose (local SherpaDesk backend + OpenClaw skill-front) matches the bundled code and runtime instructions, but the package metadata omits expected credential and install declarations and the bundle will install/run a persistent local service — these mismatches merit caution before installing.

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md and README clearly describe a backend that authenticates to SherpaDesk and requires an API token and local runtime state. Yet the registry metadata lists no required environment variables or primary credential. The bundle is not purely 'instruction-only' — it includes a full Python implementation (src/, scripts/, pyproject.toml) that implements networked API access, DB storage, and a background service. The declared metadata is therefore incomplete and inconsistent with the skill's actual purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are focused and consistent with the stated purpose: use scripts/run.py commands, bootstrap the runtime, configure a SherpaDesk API token via `configure --api-key`, seed the local DB, and optionally install a user-level systemd service. The instructions reference only skill-local paths ('.SherpaMind/') and the SherpaDesk API host. They do not direct the agent to read unrelated system files or exfiltrate data to unknown endpoints. However, they do instruct creation of local runtime state and a persistent service which affects system behavior.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Registry shows no install spec, but the repo contains bootstrap (scripts/bootstrap.py) and run (scripts/run.py) entrypoints and a pyproject/requirements, so following the SKILL.md will create a Python venv and install packages from PyPI and may register a systemd user unit. The absence of an explicit install spec in the registry combined with executable bootstrap code is an inconsistency worth flagging: running bootstrap will write files, install packages (network downloads), and create persistent artifacts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill clearly needs a SherpaDesk API token (SKILL.md shows `configure --api-key <token>`), plus skill-local config (`.SherpaMind/private/config.env`) and configurable runtime env vars (SHERPAMIND_* settings in operator notes). Yet the registry metadata lists no required env vars or primary credential. This under-declaration hides the fact that secrets (API token, org/instance keys) are necessary and will be stored locally; that mismatch is disproportionate and should be corrected.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The project intends to install a user-level persistent service (systemd --user unit) and create local state under `.SherpaMind/` (DB, public artifacts, runtime venv). That persistent presence is coherent with a local backend and is not privileged system-wide (user-level service). It's expected for this use case, but you should be aware it will run in the background and maintain local state and logs.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears to implement the described SherpaDesk backend and OpenClaw skill-front, but the registry metadata is incomplete: it does not declare the SherpaDesk API token or other env/config expectations even though the SKILL.md and code require them. Before installing: 1) Treat the bundle as code that will be executed on your host — it contains scripts that bootstrap a Python venv, install packages from PyPI, write local files under .SherpaMind/, and can register a user-level systemd service. 2) Confirm you trust the source (homepage is missing and publisher origin is unknown). 3) Review the code (client.py, scripts/bootstrap.py, scripts/run.py) to verify where API keys will be stored (SKILL.md indicates `.SherpaMind/private/config.env`) and that no unexpected external endpoints are contacted beyond SherpaDesk and the project GitHub. 4) Expect to supply a SherpaDesk API token and org/instance keys; ask the publisher/registry to update required env/credential metadata before installation. 5) If you want to limit blast radius, run bootstrap/setup in an isolated environment (non-privileged user account or VM/container) and inspect the created systemd unit and files before enabling the service. If you need more confidence, provide me with the contents of scripts/bootstrap.py and scripts/run.py and I can highlight exact commands that will be executed and any network or filesystem side effects.
